title: Chas Teaches Click (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word cabaret 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan male vocal absurdist observational comedy language lesson warm
lyrics:
[Intro - piano bar, dry and expectant]
Right, so.
We're going to learn some click consonants.
This is going to go well.

[Verse 1]
There are three main clicks in Xhosa and Zulu
The dental click, the lateral, and the palatal
Chas has a sheet of paper
And a glass of water
And the confidence of a man
Who has never attempted this before

[Verse 2]
The dental click is the tutting sound
The one English speakers use to express disappointment
The Xhosa use it to say words
This is a significant difference
Chas demonstrates
The room is politely quiet
The dental click sounds exactly like
Someone who's just remembered they left the oven on

[Pre-Chorus]
Chas moves to the lateral
Which is the sound you make
When you've bitten your tongue
And are trying not to swear
In front of someone's grandmother
He does this with great commitment

[Chorus]
Click
That's not quite it
Click
Getting closer to something
Click
The room reassures him
Click
He is doing beautifully
Click
In the way that a man is doing beautifully
When he is clearly not doing it
But everyone loves him anyway

[Bridge - spoken, completely level]
Joel tried it.
Joel got it on the second go.
Chas looked at Joel for a long moment.
Then he took another sip of water.
Then he tried again.
The click he produced
Was technically a different language entirely.
But it was said with tremendous sincerity.
And sincerity, it turns out, is most of it.

[Chorus reprise]
Click
He's getting it now
Click
The family encourages him
Click
Kerri is very patient
Click
This is actually a lesson
Click
Chas has been at it
For forty-five minutes

[Outro - piano alone, warm]
Chas can now produce
Three different sounds
None of which are the correct clicks
But two of which
Are genuinely impressive
And one of which
Has no name in any language
But everyone agreed
It should
